# 0118. A task analysis is a five-chapter design doc, written with the analysis skill; file sections land…

## Context and Problem Statement

Task #172: feat(analysis): one model, a chaptered design doc; an analysis skill adapted from mattpocock/skills.

## Considered Options

- One model: context, goals, design, alternatives, risks.
Alternatives: file-only analyses with ANALYSIS_CHAPTERS dropped. This was rejected because chapters give every task the same shape to read and to study. MCP-only analyses were rejected because agents write plans as files, and those would be lost.

## Decision Outcome

A task analysis is a five-chapter design doc, written with the analysis skill; file sections land in the chapter their heading names

Context: the rule (.claude/rules/docs.md) and ANALYSIS_CHAPTERS described a chaptered mini design doc. The code, however, made one section per `##` of each file with no chapter. MCP-written sections could also collide with file-section keys (`<file>--<heading>`).

Decision:

- One model: context, goals, design, alternatives, risks.
- Agents write the analysis with a new `analysis` skill, using one section per chapter key (`doc_section_upsert {kind: analysis, key: <chapter>, chapter}`). The skill is adapted from mattpocock/skills (to-spec, grilling, domain-modeling, research; see skills/analysis/NOTICE.md).
- Files the agent writes (plans, spikes, notes) are still read in automatically, and `ingest` now sets each section's chapter from its heading (`chapterOf`). Unmatched headings go to design.
- MCP refuses analysis keys containing `--`, which are reserved for file sections.

Alternatives: file-only analyses with ANALYSIS_CHAPTERS dropped. This was rejected because chapters give every task the same shape to read and to study. MCP-only analyses were rejected because agents write plans as files, and those would be lost.

Consequence: existing file sections get their chapter the next time their file changes. Older sections keep no chapter until then.

## Consequences

Consequence: existing file sections get their chapter the next time their file changes. Older sections keep no chapter until then.
